title: Ingredients
content:
Ingredients

What is in it, and what it does

Eight things worth knowing, written out in full. If a bottle has one of these in it, the number on the front is how much.

Vitamin B3. At 10% it calms redness, helps the skin hold water and evens tone over a couple of months. It is the least glamorous active on the shelf and the one that suits the most faces.

A humectant: it holds water. It needs water to hold, which is why it goes on damp skin and gets sealed with a moisturiser. On its own, in a dry room, it can make skin feel tighter.

A step closer to the active form than retinol, so a smaller number does the same work with less irritation. It is destroyed by light, which is why it is in an amber bottle and not a clear one.

Oil-soluble, so it gets inside a pore rather than working on the surface. Good for blocked pores and the bumps that come with them, and easy to overdo.

The mortar between skin cells. Skin that is flaky, tight or stinging when you put things on it is usually short of them.

An emollient from olives. One ingredient, no smell, no reaction in almost anyone, which is why it is in half the shelf and on its own in one bottle.

The most boring, most useful humectant there is. It is near the top of most of these labels and it is not a filler.

A mineral filter that sits on skin and reflects. In the serum it is there at 1% to help with oil, not for sun protection -- that is what the tube is for.

What we leave out

Not as a claim to virtue: each of these is left out for a reason we can say in one line.

  • Fragrance, and the essential oils people use instead of admitting it is fragrance
  • Denatured alcohol, which makes a serum feel fast and a face feel tight
  • Colour, in anything
  • Claims about cells, which we cannot prove and neither can anyone else

title: The routine
content:
The routine

Four steps in the morning, four at night

Most of a routine is the order and the frequency. This is ours, and it is shorter than you expect.

Before the day

Morning

01

Wash, or just rinse

If you cleansed last night, warm water is enough. Oily skin, use the gel.

02

Barrier serum

Four drops, pressed in rather than rubbed. Give it a minute.

03

Moisturiser

Gel cream in summer, balm in winter. Enough to stop the next step dragging.

04

Sunscreen

Two fingers' length for face and neck. This is the step that pays for the others.

After it

Evening

01

Take the day off

Cleanse twice if you wore sunscreen: once to break it up, once to wash it off.

02

Treat, on the nights you treat

Retinal twice a week, acid twice a week, never the same night.

03

Serum

Barrier serum on the nights you are not treating. Hydrating serum on damp skin.

04

Seal it

Balm last. If your skin is fine without it, skip it: it is not a moral failing.

A rough guide

How often

Cleanser

Twice a day, or once if your skin is dry

Barrier serum

Twice a day, every day

Hydrating serum

On damp skin, whenever it feels tight

Retinal

Twice a week to start, four times if it suits you

Exfoliating toner

Twice a week, never on a retinal night

Sunscreen

Every morning, all year, reapply at noon

If you only do two things

Sunscreen in the morning and a moisturiser at night will do more than any serum on this shelf. Everything else is an improvement on a routine that already exists, which is why we would rather sell you a $26 tube than a $48 bottle.

title: The lab
content:
The lab

A small room, a set of scales and a lot of dating labels

Dew is four people making a dozen products in California. Everything is mixed, filled and labelled here.

How it is made

Four hundred bottles at a time

A batch of four hundred takes a morning. It also means a formula can be changed the week we learn something, instead of waiting out a year of stock, and that every bottle can carry the date it was filled rather than a best-before that means nothing.

  • Mixed, filled and labelled in one room
  • Every bottle dated, not just batch-coded
  • Nothing tested on animals, and nothing sold where that is required
Read the ingredients

About us

400 bottles

What we will not say

That anything here repairs, renews or rebuilds. Skin is not a wall. These are well-made basics at strengths that have been studied, and the difference between a good routine and a bad one is mostly whether you use it.

title: FAQ
content:
Help

Questions we are asked most

What to start with, what not to mix, and what happens if it does not suit you.

Choosing

The barrier serum, a moisturiser and the sunscreen. That is a whole routine, and it is the one we would buy first.

Gel if your face is oily or you wear sunscreen daily; cream if washing leaves your skin tight. If you are between the two, the gel.

All of it is fragrance-free, which is the single biggest cause of reactions. The acid and the retinal are the two to introduce slowly.

Using it

Not on the same night. Alternate them, and skip both if your skin is stinging.

The serum, about six weeks for tone. The acid, a fortnight for texture. Sunscreen works the day you start.

No. It is a modern filter blend rather than a mineral one, which is also why it does not sting eyes.

A patch test of whatever you ordered. Behind the ear, three days, before it goes near your face.

Orders

Yes, within sixty days. Skincare cannot be judged unopened, so a return policy that requires a seal is a policy against being used.

Six months for the serums, twelve for the balm and the oil. The date on the back is when it was filled.

Not yet. The sunscreen is regulated differently almost everywhere, and shipping a partial routine seemed worse than waiting.

title: Delivery and returns
content:
Delivery and returns

Sixty days, opened or not

Skincare cannot be judged through a seal, so a policy that requires one is a policy against trying it.

What it costs

Delivery

Standard delivery

$5, two to four working days

Free delivery

On orders over $45

Express

$12, next working day if ordered before noon

Returns

Sixty days, opened or not

Samples

Three sachets with every order

Returns

Sixty days from delivery, whether or not it has been opened. Tell us what it did and we will refund it: a bottle that did not suit you is worth more to us as a sentence than as stock.

If it reacts

Stop using it, and email us before you throw it away. Nine times out of ten it is the acid or the retinal introduced too fast, and the fix is frequency rather than a different bottle.

Damaged in the post

Photograph the box within 48 hours and we will send another. Glass travels in a moulded insert, but couriers are couriers.
